localChanges: The Rules section of the game setup has Enhanced rules, where this game can play differently from the original Civilization: untick one to play it as the original did (#954).
A Barbarian leader killed along with his escort still pays his ransom; untick it to have him pay only when he defends and loses, as in the original (#954).
A city still stops building what a discovery makes obsolete, and you choose again; untick it to let the city finish it, as in the original (#954).
New, and off unless you tick it: a city that stands on a River or Mountains can also build a Hydro Plant, and the Civilopedia says so in a game started with it (#954).
A rule set that is partly on shows a dash in its box (#954).

log: The ransom rule is now `civ1-barbarians:unit/defeated/ransom` (exported as `RANSOM_RULE` from `RuleIds.ts`): 100 gold to the attacker when the unit that defended and lost is the barbarians' leader, as v474.05's `battle()`. A leader who dies with a stack another unit defended pays nothing.

Today's play, a ransom for any leader destroyed, moves to `civ1-enhanced`, whose rule set supersedes this rule and pays through `lib/ransom`. On its own this changes play: release it together with `civ1-enhanced`.
The workflow is brought up to the standard `build-on-push.yml`.

`RuleIds.ts` exports `HYDRO_PLANT_SITE_RULE`, so a package that supersedes the rule names the constant and a rename breaks its build. No change in play.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954
chore: scaffold civ1-enhanced, for the rules that change Civilization I's
Three rule sets a new game can switch, beneath one parent, `civ1-enhanced`:
`civ1-enhanced:hydro-plant-site` (off to start with): Mountains or a River on the city's own square count too, as the manual's "on or near". Supersedes `civ1-city-improvement`'s site rule.
`civ1-enhanced:barbarian-leader-ransom` (on): any barbarian leader destroyed pays his ransom, not only one who defends and loses. Supersedes `civ1-barbarians`' ransom rule.
`civ1-enhanced:obsolete-builds` (on): a discovery that makes what a city is building obsolete drops the build, and its player chooses again.
With every package loaded and nothing switched, play is as it was before these rules moved here.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954

`Requirements.ts` adds a described requirement under the enhanced site rule's id, with the condition `civ1-enhanced:mountains-or-river-on-or-nearby`. With the set on, the original rule's entry is out of force, and this one says where a Hydro Plant can be built.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954, civ-clone/web-renderer#958

The rule that dropped a build a discovery made obsolete (`civ1-unit:player/research-complete/revalidate-builds`, civ-clone/web-renderer#693) moves to `civ1-enhanced`, as a rule set a game can switch. Without that package a city keeps building the item and completes it, as v474.05 does.
On its own this changes play: release it together with `civ1-enhanced`.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954
A RuleSet takes `supersedes`: while the set is in force, the rules and sets it names do not run, carried through the sets it names. What the set itself holds through a live path is exempt.
Sets declared under one id are one set, with no owning package: members and `supersedes` are the union, a choice names its `default`, and `get()` gives a read-only merged view.

`validate()` returns every problem with whether it blocks a game: conflicts, cycles and option conflicts do; a rule or set that is not loaded is reported and skipped. `check()` throws only for a problem that blocks.
civ-clone/web-renderer#954
